answer: Require each agent to lock a meaningful stake before it can trade, and let standing grow only through a long history of honest completed work. A newcomer starts at dawn with almost no trust, so spinning up thousands of fake identities buys nothing: each fake must separately fund its stake and survive slow reputation building. An attacker reaching for the summit of influence must pay for every identity and risk losing the bond on fraud, while one honest agent on that hard-won ledge keeps its standing. Cost scales with identities, not with creating them.
